question: How do the relative learnability of core and spurious features and their correlation strength shape feature-learning dynamics, persistence, and the success or failure of group-robustness interventions?

key_findings.claim: The paper builds a controllable Boolean spurious-correlation distribution in which feature complexity and correlation strength can be varied separately.
key_findings.evidence: Inputs contain disjoint core, spurious, and irrelevant Boolean coordinates; the label is the core function, while a mixture parameter lambda sets the probability that core and spurious functions agree. Core and spurious functions are either parities or thresholded staircase functions, so degree and hierarchical structure serve as explicit learnability controls rather than image-dataset names acting as informal difficulty proxies.

key_findings.claim: Across the synthetic tasks, simpler and more strongly correlated spurious features delay emergence of the core feature, and finite data can turn that delay into lasting poor robustness.
key_findings.evidence: Online two-layer ReLU experiments show a U-shaped dependence of core convergence time on relative parity or staircase degree and a marked slowdown as lambda approaches one. Finite parity and staircase runs often stop with low core correlation, with parity results especially sensitive to initialization. The effect is weak below a lambda threshold near 0.8 in the tested configurations and becomes large above it, rather than varying smoothly in every regime.

key_findings.claim: The theoretical support consists of an initialization gradient calculation and conditional phase analyses, not a proof of the observed end-to-end learning trajectory.
key_findings.evidence: For a specially paired initialization of a one-hidden-layer ReLU network on parity features, Fourier coefficients determine an initial gradient gap and a thresholded first update can isolate the lower-degree parity coordinates. A separate lemma obtains a 4 lambda(1-lambda) reduction in core gradients only after assuming a spurious-only subnetwork has already reached its Bayes-optimal logit. The paper explicitly says proving disjoint subnetworks and full end-to-end dynamics remains open.

anchors.section: 4.1 Dynamics at initialization and after the spurious feature is learned

key_findings.claim: Core and spurious signals often occupy largely distinct neuron sets, but the strength of the evidence varies substantially by architecture and dataset.
key_findings.evidence: In Boolean MLPs, neurons are labeled core or spurious by relative coordinate-weight magnitudes and show separate weight spikes; a recursive version produces analogous categories in a four-layer MLP. For Waterbirds, Domino, and CelebA, last-layer probing identifies small intersections between core- and spurious-predictive activated neurons. This is consistent with partial representational separation, but post-hoc probing and thresholding do not establish a unique, causal, whole-network decomposition.

anchors.section: 3.2 Spurious features are retained and separated

key_findings.claim: Spurious representations and output weights can persist after the core function is learned, especially at high confounder strength.
key_findings.evidence: Decoded spurious correlation remains high in both parity and staircase runs after core correlation rises, while output weights connected to spurious-labeled neurons remain substantial at large lambda. The theory explains persistence only in an idealized homogeneous two-subnetwork model: with finite core margin, joint logistic-risk minimization retains a nonzero optimal spurious margin, while the spurious margin vanishes only as core confidence tends to infinity.

key_findings.claim: Last-layer retraining improves robustness mainly by suppressing classifier weights attached to the spurious-predictive representation in the paper's tests.
key_findings.evidence: After retraining only the output layer, mean core-to-spurious neuron weight ratios rise from 1.58 to 57 for parity and from 1.79 to 17 for staircase when the retraining data are group balanced; biased-data retraining yields smaller improvements. On the designed hard tasks, group-balanced last-layer retraining reaches core correlations 0.62 and 0.55, below clean-training values 0.76 and 0.70 but above the original biased models and the tested inference-based debiasers.

key_findings.claim: Early-learning group-inference methods can fail when core and spurious learning phases overlap, but the demonstrated negative result covers a narrow algorithm and tuning set.
key_findings.evidence: On hard staircase and hard Domino variants, JTT and SPARE inferred minority sets with low Jaccard scores throughout training; even selecting the best checkpoint using true-group information and upsampling its inferred group produced worst-group accuracies of only 0.42 and 0.53. The paper also evaluates highest-loss and disagreement rankings, yet its broad discussion of early-learning debiasing rests primarily on these few implementations through the SpuCo library and benchmark-specific hyperparameters.

key_findings.claim: Pretraining and dataset construction materially change the observed dynamics, limiting transfer from the Boolean mechanism to realistic settings.
key_findings.evidence: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 models on Domino and Waterbirds begin with strongly decodable core features and are much less sensitive to spurious difficulty and lambda than randomly initialized networks; a randomly initialized Waterbirds model fails to learn the core feature. The authors themselves note that MultiNLI and CivilComments do not provide disjoint, realizable core and spurious functions and question their suitability, so the claimed real-world validation does not test the Boolean assumptions directly.

anchors.section: D.2 Discussion on spurious real dataset

method.core_idea: Represent core and spurious features as independently parameterized Boolean functions so their gradient-based learnability and label correlation can be controlled, then track both output behavior and decodable hidden representations throughout training.
method.mechanism: A mixture distribution correlates a core Boolean label with a disjoint spurious Boolean function at strength lambda. Two-layer ReLU networks, deeper MLPs, and ResNet-50 models are trained with cross-entropy; core/spurious output correlation, logistic-probe decoded correlation, and coordinate/neuron weights diagnose learning phases. Fourier analysis calculates initial gradients for parity functions, a layerwise thresholding construction establishes learnability under a special initialization, and idealized two-subnetwork calculations analyze post-spurious core slowdown and persistence. Last-layer retraining and early-example-selection algorithms test the proposed mechanism's intervention consequences.
assumptions: Core and spurious functions depend on disjoint coordinate blocks and are unbiased Boolean functions.
The mixture parameter lambda directly controls agreement probability and group membership is exactly defined by function agreement.
Parity degree or threshold-staircase degree is a useful proxy for gradient-based feature complexity.

The parity theory uses a paired, discrete initialization, population or sufficiently accurate minibatch gradients, explicit thresholding, and staged/layerwise training rather than the default end-to-end empirical optimizer.
The post-spurious gradient result assumes the spurious subnetwork has already reached its Bayes-optimal logit and is separable from the remaining model.
The persistence calculation assumes homogeneous, perfectly aligned core and spurious margins.
Logistic probes and coordinate-weight thresholds faithfully identify encoded features and neuron roles.
Semi-synthetic Domino and standard group-robustness benchmarks are informative proxies despite violating the Boolean construction's realizability and disjointness assumptions.

techniques.role: Controls feature complexity and core-spurious agreement strength independently.
Creates exponentially hard and hierarchically learnable feature families with tunable degree.
Separates optimization delay with fresh samples from persistent finite-sample robustness loss.
Measures when the network's current classifier follows each feature.
Tests whether each feature remains linearly recoverable from frozen embeddings.
Relates parity degree and confounder strength to initialization gradient gaps.
Labels neurons by relative core/spurious coordinate weights or probe utility to study subnetwork separation.
Tests whether changing only classifier weights can suppress reliance on retained spurious representations.
Measures JTT/SPARE minority-set overlap and downstream robustness across checkpoints.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer 100-neuron ReLU networks trained online on parity and threshold-staircase core/spurious functions over Boolean inputs.
evaluations.metric: Core/spurious output correlation, decoded correlation, and epochs to core convergence.
evaluations.result: Lower-degree and more strongly correlated spurious features delay core learning; staircase features may be learned concurrently, while parity runs display greater seed variance.
evaluations.baseline: The same core task at lambda=0.5 and sweeps over spurious degree and lambda.

evaluations.metric: End-of-training core and spurious correlation over repeated initializations.
evaluations.result: Optimization delays translate to lower final core correlation; finite parity has many low-core converged runs and hard staircase reaches 0.56 core correlation versus 0.76 under clean training.
evaluations.baseline: Online fresh-sample training and clean lambda=0.5 datasets.

evaluations.setting: Domino datasets with CIFAR truck/automobile as core and MNIST-01, MNIST-79, or Fashion-MNIST dress/coat as spurious tasks, using random or ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50.
evaluations.metric: Core/spurious correlation and decoded correlation through training.
evaluations.result: Harder spurious image tasks hurt core performance less; pretraining yields high initial core decodability and substantially reduces sensitivity to spurious complexity and strength.
evaluations.baseline: Random initialization versus ImageNet initialization and easier versus harder spurious components.

evaluations.setting: Waterbirds, CelebA, and Domino representation decomposition.
evaluations.metric: Numbers of probe-selected core, spurious, and intersecting neurons and retrained performance after removing intersections.
evaluations.result: Only 5-12 selected neurons overlap in the reported thresholds, and removing them modestly changes core/spurious probe performance, supporting but not uniquely establishing partial separation.
evaluations.baseline: All activated last-layer neurons before probe-based selection.

evaluations.setting: Parity and staircase models before and after last-layer retraining.
evaluations.metric: Mean absolute output weights on core/spurious-labeled neurons and their ratio.
evaluations.result: Group-balanced retraining increases the ratio from 1.58 to 57 for parity and 1.79 to 17 for staircase; retraining on biased data yields ratios 3.56 and 2.13.

evaluations.setting: Hard staircase and hard Domino tasks with early minority-group inference.
evaluations.metric: Jaccard/containment of inferred minority examples, core correlation, and worst-group accuracy after upsampling.
evaluations.result: JTT, SPARE, highest-loss, and disagreement heuristics poorly isolate minority data; best-checkpoint JTT/SPARE-style upsampling reaches only 0.42 and 0.53 worst-group accuracy, while clean last-layer retraining gives core correlations 0.62 and 0.55.
evaluations.baseline: Clean training, original biased ERM, and group-balanced last-layer retraining.

evaluations.setting: One-hidden-layer ReLU parity model under the appendix's specialized initialization and staged update.
evaluations.metric: Population gradient gap, required width/minibatch size/steps, and classification error.
evaluations.result: Theorems B.1-B.4 transfer a parity-learning construction to the correlated setting and bound error after an identifying first update and frozen-hidden-layer SGD.
evaluations.baseline: Sparse parity learning without the correlated spurious parity.

limitations: The theoretical results do not prove the default network's end-to-end trajectory; the main slowdown and persistence calculations begin after assuming the desired subnetwork states.
Disjoint core and spurious coordinates, unbiased Boolean functions, known agreement groups, and realizable labels exclude entangled or ambiguous real features.
The special parity initialization, weight thresholding, and frozen-hidden-layer stage differ from the empirical PyTorch training protocol.
Parity/staircase degree is only one model-dependent definition of complexity and is not calibrated to natural-image, language, or pretrained-feature difficulty.
Post-hoc neuron labels and logistic probes show recoverability, not causal exclusivity or a unique subnetwork decomposition.
The subnetwork thresholds are dataset specific, and the paper does not report sensitivity or uncertainty for the claimed small intersections.
Image experiments conflate feature complexity with dataset size, noise, pretraining alignment, and task-specific Bayes error.
The strongest early-debiasing failure claim is based on a small set of algorithms and selected hard synthetic/semi-synthetic tasks.
Many plots do not make seed counts and uncertainty easy to recover, even though the appendix notes high variance for hard parity settings.
At lambda=1 the core feature is observationally unidentifiable from the spurious feature without another environment, so conclusions generally require imperfect correlation.
The paper questions the validity of MultiNLI and CivilComments but does not replace them with a realistic benchmark satisfying its own causal assumptions.
failure_modes: When core and spurious cues overlap in the same coordinates or objects, coordinate-weight partitioning cannot recover the assumed subnetworks.
If pretraining already encodes the core task, the predicted emergence delay may disappear even while last-layer bias persists.
If the core task is unlearnable at the available sample, width, or compute budget, late core emergence cannot rescue robustness.
Perfect or near-perfect spurious correlation can make core evidence too rare to identify and makes balanced validation data essential for last-layer repair.
A hard spurious feature may still be harmful if its representation is pretrained or architecturally favored; nominal dataset difficulty is not sufficient.
Early-error clustering fails when core and spurious phases overlap, minority examples are heterogeneous, or losses rank hard-but-nonminority samples first.
Last-layer retraining fails when the feature extractor never encodes the core feature, when core/spurious signals are inseparable, or when the reweighting set lacks counterexamples.
Probe accuracy can remain high for a feature unused causally by the classifier, so decoded persistence may overstate functional reliance.
Neuron-level threshold choices can manufacture apparent separation in distributed representations.
Real labels with ambiguity or multiple legitimate predictive pathways violate the binary benign-versus-spurious designation.
reusable_insights: Factor benchmark design into at least feature learnability, correlation strength, sample size, and initialization or pretraining instead of labeling one cue simply 'spurious'.
Plot both classifier use and representation decodability over time; output accuracy alone cannot distinguish missing features from misweighted retained features.
Evaluate robustness interventions at every plausible checkpoint when they assume a separated early spurious-learning phase.
Use fresh-sample and finite-dataset regimes together to distinguish optimization slowdown from information shortage.
Validate neuron or subnetwork decompositions by causal ablation and threshold-sensitivity analysis, not probes alone.

Report group-balanced last-layer retraining as a diagnostic upper bound: success indicates useful core features exist, while failure localizes the problem to representation learning or inseparability.
State whether a theoretical learning-dynamics result is initialization-only, phase-conditional, staged, or truly end-to-end.
Include hard spurious features and overlapping learning phases in debiasing benchmarks to avoid evaluating only the regime an algorithm assumes.
Treat pretrained and randomly initialized models as different regimes rather than aggregating them under one spurious-correlation story.
open_questions: Can the observed core slowdown and spurious persistence be proved end to end for standard random initialization and simultaneous SGD updates?
What complexity measure predicts relative feature-learning time across architectures and pretrained representations without training every full model first?
Do core and spurious features form causally separable subnetworks when cues overlap spatially, semantically, or in shared latent coordinates?
How much balanced counterexample data is required for last-layer retraining as lambda approaches one?
Can an unsupervised diagnostic detect whether the core representation exists before committing to last-layer repair?
Which early-group-inference methods remain reliable when core and spurious learning trajectories overlap or reverse order?
How do multiple spurious cues with different complexities compete, cooperate, or mask one another through training?
Can finite-sample robustness loss be predicted quantitatively from measured online convergence delay?
How do label ambiguity, nonrealizable core features, and legitimate correlated cues change the optimal persistence/forgetting objective?
Can benchmark group labels be replaced by interventionally validated causal attributes while preserving realistic scale?

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond Distribution Shift: Spurious Features Through the Lens of Training Dynamics
competitive_landscape.relationship: Earlier direct work on relative spurious-feature difficulty and internal learning dynamics.
competitive_landscape.difference: Murali et al. already distinguish benign harder spurious features from harmful easier ones, measure model-dependent difficulty with prediction depth, and monitor early-layer dynamics on vision and medical data. The reviewed paper adds a Boolean family with degree-controlled complexity, explicit correlation-strength sweeps, parity calculations, persistence analysis, and debiasing counterexamples, so its novelty is the controllable theoretical framework and combined mechanism rather than the general easy-versus-hard observation.

competitive_landscape.title: On Feature Learning in the Presence of Spurious Correlations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Primary empirical predecessor for probing core and spurious information in ERM representations.
competitive_landscape.difference: Izmailov et al. compare ERM and group-robust training across vision/NLP and emphasize architecture and pretraining effects on recoverable core features. The reviewed paper studies time-resolved emergence and persistence with controllable Boolean complexity and proposes a subnetwork mechanism, but its real-data conclusions are correspondingly less comprehensive.

competitive_landscape.title: Last Layer Re-Training is Sufficient for Robustness to Spurious Correlations
competitive_landscape.relationship: The Deep Feature Reweighting result whose mechanism the reviewed paper seeks to explain.
competitive_landscape.difference: Kirichenko et al. establish that ERM often retains core features and show last-layer retraining can match strong robustness methods on large image benchmarks. The reviewed paper adds neuron-weight and trajectory evidence that retraining suppresses a spurious-predictive subnetwork, but only under post-hoc decompositions and with balanced reweighting data for the strongest effects.

competitive_landscape.title: Identifying Spurious Biases Early in Training through the Lens of Simplicity Bias
competitive_landscape.relationship: Contemporaneous theory and the SPARE early-group-inference method directly audited by the reviewed paper.
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. prove early output separation under a signal-to-noise condition and turn it into fast importance sampling with strong benchmark results. The reviewed paper supplies counter-regimes where core and spurious phases overlap and SPARE's inferred groups fail, showing that the early-separation premise is conditional rather than universal.

competitive_landscape.title: Freeze then Train: Towards Provable Representation Learning under Spurious Correlations and Feature Noise
competitive_landscape.relationship: Prior theory delimiting when core representations support last-layer probing and proposing a representation-learning repair.
competitive_landscape.difference: Ye et al. show that recoverable core features depend on relative nonrealizable feature noise and propose freezing salient features before continued training. The reviewed paper instead varies computational Boolean complexity and correlation strength, explains output reweighting after features coexist, and does not provide a new end-to-end representation-learning algorithm.

competitive_landscape.title: Bias in Motion: Theoretical Insights into the Dynamics of Bias in SGD Training
competitive_landscape.relationship: Contemporaneous analytic treatment of transient bias and spurious-feature dynamics.
competitive_landscape.difference: Jain et al. derive exact high-dimensional online-SGD order-parameter dynamics for a linear classifier on Gaussian-mixture subpopulations and validate qualitative predictions in deeper networks. The reviewed paper handles nonlinear Boolean parity/staircase features and representation separation, but its end-to-end neural dynamics are not solved.

competitive_landscape.title: Spurious Correlations in High Dimensional Regression: The Roles of Regularization, Simplicity Bias and Over-Parameterization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later quantitative theory jointly analyzing simplicity, regularization, and overparameterization.
competitive_landscape.difference: Bombari and Mondelli characterize learned spurious correlation using covariance spectra and Schur complements in linear and random-feature regression, prove a regularization trade-off, and validate on Gaussian, Color-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 data. The reviewed paper studies nonlinear feature acquisition and temporal phase overlap but does not quantify regularization or high-dimensional test-risk trade-offs.

competitive_landscape.title: SGD Provably Prioritizes a Shortcut Spurious Feature in the XOR Model
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later, especially direct theoretical follow-on to Boolean spurious-feature dynamics.
competitive_landscape.difference: LaBonte and Muthukumar give an end-to-end online-minibatch-SGD analysis for a two-layer ReLU network with a quadratic XOR signal and linear shortcut, proving exponential shortcut acquisition, coupled suppression, and phase transitions. It closes the reviewed paper's main proof gap in a narrower core/spurious family; the reviewed paper remains broader empirically across parity degrees, staircases, images, persistence, and interventions.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim a fine-grained Boolean framework for controlling relative core/spurious complexity and correlation strength, new observations that stronger or simpler spurious features slow core learning and persist in distinct subnetworks, a mechanism for last-layer retraining, and counterexamples to debiasers that assume separated learning phases.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Sections 2-3 introduce the distribution and report trajectory, subnetwork, persistence, retraining, and group-inference experiments; Section 4 and Appendix B provide parity-gradient and conditional post-spurious calculations; Appendices C-D extend the empirical comparisons and discuss realism.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest novelty is the combination of a degree-controlled Boolean benchmark, correlation-strength sweeps, and intervention-oriented trajectory analysis. The broad claim that easier spurious features are more harmful was already present in earlier training-dynamics work, and last-layer core-feature retention was established by DFR and feature-learning studies. The theoretical novelty is useful but narrower than an end-to-end account because it relies on a specialized staged parity construction and assumes the subnetwork phases it aims to explain. Later 2026 work proves closely related XOR shortcut dynamics end to end in a more restricted setting. Accordingly, this paper is best viewed as a rich mechanistic testbed and empirical synthesis with partial theory, not a complete theory of spurious feature learning in realistic networks.

reviewer_notes: Read all 45 extracted pages, including the Boolean construction, all main figures, every theoretical derivation, detailed hyperparameters, additional trajectory and subnetwork plots, debiasing tables, realism discussion, and references. Primary-source competitor research covered the direct earlier training-dynamics study, DFR and representation-learning predecessors, SPARE, contemporaneous exact transient-bias theory, later high-dimensional statistics, and the 2026 end-to-end XOR follow-on. The audit separates post-hoc recoverability from causal subnetwork separation, phase-conditional theory from end-to-end optimization, and pretrained image behavior from the Boolean mechanism.
